$description: Layout — grid (web/app margin/gutter/columns) + border-width + border-radius, re-based from Figma native export (collection 'semantic-scale', modes scale-1/2/3). Breakpoint definitions and scale->viewport mapping are PRESERVED from the Breakpoints-page doc (not carried in the variable export). Source: _raw/semantic-scale/.

scale.$description: Responsive scale modes (Figma variable modes). AUTHORITATIVE viewport mapping (Dave): scale-1 = 320-959, scale-2 = 960-1599, scale-3 = 1600+. Plus scale-1-200 = 200% accessibility text-zoom variant of scale-1 (see typography.json).

bento.$description: BENTO — the canon structural grammar (MINTED s217-D2, #217, Dave, 2026-08-23, from Dave's four per-theme tuner exports off knowledge/_fitness-test/bento-tuner-v1.html). One grammar serves all four bento types: presets, gallery (incl. aspect-mapped photography spans), container-query full-scale, and snap-designer output. GUTTER IS THE ONLY PER-THEME DIVERGENCE — supercharge + mono 0px (this base), legacy + console 24px (their override sets). Everything else is SHARED across the four themes and lives here once. The RADIUS is deliberately NOT here: s217-D2 puts the theme radius on the bento's OUTER CONTAINER, and that role already has a home — border-radius/container. Consumed by canon/gen_canon_bento.py, which compiles this group into the AUTO-BENTO block of canon/canon.css (concrete container-query literals; s200-D1 mint-time derivation — nothing resolved at runtime that a container query cannot read).

columns.$note: MINTED s217-D2. Track count at the widest band. Per-instance overridable via --bento-columns (that is how a nested bento carries its own parameter set).

gutter.$note: MINTED s217-D2 — BASE tier (mono is the base theme; supercharge inherits it). ⚠ THE ONLY PER-THEME BENTO DIVERGENCE: legacy and console override this to 24px in their own override sets. A theme override that never lands leaves THIS value silently in force, so the gutter is measured in every theme, never inferred from one (#217 probe).

outer-padding.$note: MINTED s217-D2 — shared across all four themes (all four tuner exports read 0). Padding INSIDE the bento container, between the container edge and the grid.

row-unit.$note: MINTED s217-D2 — shared. grid-auto-rows. ⚠ FIXED rows, not intrinsic: with intrinsic rows the tallest content sizes every row and the span vocabulary renders invisible (MEASURED #217 on the Foundations photography bento).

packing.$note: MINTED s217-D2 — dense packing ON, shared. grid-auto-flow. Per-instance `--bento-packing: row` turns it off without a new class. ⚠ ENCODED s217-D4 (ds-051) ON THE s141-D1 PRECEDENT: `row dense` is a CSS KEYWORD and there is no W3C DTCG type for one — carrying `$type:"string"` made this a token the DTCG gate had to fail (DTCG-001), and there is no honest numeric stand-in. So the value is preserved VERBATIM under $extensions["com.apollo.sds"] exactly as s141-D1 (B) preserved the scale breakpoint sets, and the $value is GONE: with no $value this node is a GROUP, not a token, so no DTCG check applies to it. THE EMITTED CSS IS UNCHANGED — gen_canon_tokens.py reads the cssKeyword carrier and still emits `--layout-bento-packing: row dense;` in the same place. Storage moved; output did not.

caption-space.$note: MINTED s217-D3 — the GALLERY role's caption block, ruled 'more generous' (Dave, #217: 'lets be more generous with the caption space'). ⚠ NOT A TASTE PICK — DERIVED, and every term is an existing number measured off the shipped page. TODAY the gallery caption measures 62px: padding-block 8 + 8, a description on `.t-ed-caption` (12/16) clamped to TWO lines = 32, a 2px gap, and a licence line on `.t-cm-legal` (12px, line-height 1) = 12. THE GENEROUS BLOCK buys ONE MORE DESCRIPTION LINE (32 → 48) and steps the padding one rung up the 4px spacing ladder (8 → 12): 12 + 48 + 2 + 12 + 12 = 86px, i.e. +24px / +38.7%. The LINE ALLOWANCE IS DERIVED BACK OUT OF THIS NUMBER at mint time (s200-D1) — (86 − 24 − 2 − 12) ÷ 16 = 3 — never carried as a second token, so the space and the clamp cannot disagree. Applies to role=gallery only; dashboard and brochureware captions are unchanged.

$bands.$description: Responsive collapse, as CONTAINER queries against the bento's own inline size (the WALL decides, not the window — that is what makes nesting work). ⚠ BUILD-TIME LITERALS BY NECESSITY: a container-query condition cannot read a custom property, so these numbers are compiled into canon.css by gen_canon_bento.py rather than emitted as vars. Dave unified the 800/820 export discrepancy: 'Make them all 820' (s217-D2).

$spanDerivation.$description: BUILD-TIME span derivation — read by generators (canon/gen_canon_bento.py exposes span_for/emphasise), never by CSS, so these are metadata keys and emit no custom property. ⚠ THE ASPECT THRESHOLDS APPLY TO THE PHOTOGRAPHY BENTO ONLY (s217-D2 in as many words): card spans are AUTHORED. Wiring thresholds onto cards would silently re-lay-out every card wall. The emphasis rhythm applies to both — it is POSITION, not preference.

$roles.$description: BENTO ROLES — MINTED s217-D3 (#217, Dave, 2026-08-23). A bento instance carries a role, and the ROLE decides where the radius sits, what the spacing is, and whether the squaring pass runs. Read by generators (canon/gen_canon_bento.py exposes role_policy()) AND compiled into canon.css as `[data-bento-role=…]` rules — metadata keys, no custom property of their own. ⚠ THE GRAMMAR IS IDENTICAL IN ALL FOUR THEMES; console is only the theme where the difference is VISIBLE, because its radius token is non-zero. Where a theme's radius is 0 the same rules resolve to 0 and nothing moves. ⚠ ROLE DOES NOT TOUCH THE SPAN DERIVATION: the aspect thresholds above (incl. the portrait two-row mapping) apply to every photography bento whatever its role — squaring and aspect mapping are DIFFERENT MECHANISMS and gallery relaxes only the first.

dashboard.$description: Sectioned app, bento-of-bentos. The s217-D2 model: the theme radius sits on each inner bento's CONTAINER and the tiles inside are square, at 1px spacing. ⚠ THE 1px IS INSIDE THE INNER BENTOS. A dashboard bento whose tiles are THEMSELVES bentos is the outer wall and keeps the theme gutter — Dave's own example is tight inner walls inside a generously spaced outer, so a blanket 1px would collapse exactly the structure the role exists to describe.

brochureware.$description: Sectioned marketing page. The tiles THEMSELVES carry the radius and the spacing; the container is square and does not clip.

gallery.$description: Page-level photography. Radius and spacing as brochureware, but the SQUARING PASS RELAXES — orphans are acceptable, the requirement is only a layout appropriate to portrait and landscape images. Carries the generous caption space above.
gallery.caption: generous

border-radius.$description: Shape tier (ADR-0010 flex slots; Dave 2026-07-21 evening: one radius CANNOT be universal — radii differ by component role, cards vs buttons; maximum flexibility, the horizon is a THEME GENERATOR where every slot is a dial). 'default' = the theme's base radius; the ROLE tokens alias it, so a theme may set ONE value (default — everything follows) or dial roles independently (Console: surface differs from control). Components bind ROLE tokens, never 'default' directly and never literals (radius gate). Role taxonomy PROVISIONAL (agent, 2026-07-21): control/surface/indicator — extend by evidence during Phase 1, not speculation. 50%/999px circle+pill idioms stay literal (deliberately round in every theme).

control.$note: Interactive elements: buttons, inputs, selects, chips/tags, selection boxes.

surface.$note: Containers: cards, dialogs/modals, menus/dropdown panels, tooltips, tables, notifications.

indicator.$note: Small status/utility marks: status chips, non-pill badges, progress tracks, kbd hints.

container.$note: Outer wrappers that HOLD other radiused things: segmented-control tracks, toolbars/segmented groups, panel shells. Distinct from 'surface' because a container's radius is the OUTER of a concentric pair — the inner thumb radius derives as container − padding (s200-D1 clause c). PROMOTED from PROPOSED SLOT to canon by s200-D2 / s200-D3 (#200, Dave, 2026-08-18); console overrides it to 20, and per s200-D3 nothing was written for mono/legacy/supercharge — they follow this base alias like every other role. ⚠ s202-D2 corrected reading (#202, Dave, 2026-08-18): the inner thumb radius no longer derives from the track PADDING — it derives from the TUNED DIAL 6, thumb = max(container − 6, 0). Padding remains a real spacing token; it simply no longer feeds the radius.

segmented-container.$description: Per-scale OUTER radius of the segmented control's concentric pair. Base = 0 (square themes: mono, legacy, supercharge). Console overrides per scale (6/8/10/12) in tokens/themes/apollo-console.overrides.json — s201-D1.

focus.$description: Keyboard focus-indicator geometry. No canonical Figma primitive — see semantic-colour.json focus group and guidelines/focus-indicators.md. SIGNED OFF as canon by Dave 2026-06-20 (was tagged review). Ring colour lives in semantic-colour.json (focus/ring).

ring-offset.$description: Gap between the element edge and the ring, px — keeps the ring clear of the component fill.

target.$description: Interactive target-size tier — the Apollo hit-area standard (RULED by Dave 2026-07-24). A control presents a hit area of at least 'min' even when its VISIBLE box is smaller; the invisible ::before target anchors within the control (9-point matrix) so it stays aligned to neighbours. 44 = HSBC default / WCAG 2.5.5 AAA / Apple HIG / IBM Carbon. Dial-down floor is 24 (WCAG 2.5.8 AA + spacing exception); never below. Reference impl: snippets/Segmented-control.reference.html (.seg button::before + .hit-*).

min.$description: Default minimum interactive target size. Controls bind --hit: var(--target-min).

size.$description: Component DIMENSION tier — total outer heights of sized controls, the dimension-first grammar Dave tuned at #200/#201 (xs/s/m/l). Distinct from `scale` (spine metadata) and from `padding` (tokens/spacing.json): a size is the OUTER box a control presents.

segmented-control.$description: Total outer height of the segmented control, per scale. BASE tier: mono is the base theme, legacy and supercharge inherit it; console overrides with the identical tuned values in tokens/themes/apollo-console.overrides.json. s202-D1 — 'the square themes inherit console's tuned segmented dimensions, and the mint is base-tier'.
segmented-control.$reconstructionNote: ⚠ PROVENANCE — RESTORED #219 (2026-08-25), lane 1. s202-D1 ruled these sizes minted at BASE alongside the radii (layout.json) and paddings (spacing.json), and the sibling families here carry a $reconstructionNote recording that an accidental `git checkout` at #202 discarded the uncommitted base mint. The radii and paddings were reconstructed at #202; THE SIZES WERE NOT, and the gap survived unseen because nothing consumed them (the canon .cn-segmented-control snippet still used its legacy 28/32/36 heights). `canon/gen_theme_cascade.py::_store_for` already routes `size/` to this file with a comment asserting this very mint. VALUES are Dave's own ruled tuner-v3 numbers (s201-D1: xs 24 · s 36 · m 44 · l 48) and are byte-identical to console's own overrides; the prose is a faithful restatement, not a byte-for-byte restore. NO NEW RULING — enactment of s202-D1.

xs.$note: RE-MINTED 28px by Dave's ruling #227 (2026-08-30) — conductor inscribes as s227-D4. — “xs is going to be 28 height”, across the board (all four themes; console’s override carries the identical number). Was 24px (MINTED s201-D1 console / s202-D1 base tier, RESTORED #219). Total outer height at scale `xs`. Concrete number on disk, no runtime derivation (s200-D1 clause a). Pairs with padding/segmented-control/xs = 2px and border-radius/segmented-container/xs. Still below the 44 hit-zone floor, so the control presents an invisible 44px target (s201-D2).

s.$note: MINTED s200-D4 (console) / s202-D1 (base tier), RESTORED #219. Total outer height at scale `s` — the tuner-v3 readout 36/2/8 Dave minted at #200. Below the 44 hit-zone floor, so the control presents an invisible 44px target (s201-D2).

m.$note: MINTED s201-D1 (console) / s202-D1 (base tier), RESTORED #219. Total outer height at scale `m`. Sits exactly ON the 44 hit-zone floor — visual height and hit target coincide (s201-D3).

l.$note: MINTED s201-D1 (console) / s202-D1 (base tier), RESTORED #219. Total outer height at scale `l`. ABOVE the 44 floor, so the hit box is NATURAL at 48 — s201-D3, Dave: 'natural for anything bigger than 44'.

min-hit-area.$note: MINTED s200-D4 (console) / s202-D1 carried to base, RESTORED #219. The segmented hit-zone FLOOR: the target is max(44, visual height) — s201-D2 (hit zone, not visual height) + s201-D3 (natural above the floor). ⚠ DUPLICATE OF `target/min` (44px), which is what the reference implementation actually binds via --hit; this token is the segmented-specific name the tuner-v3 export used. Reconciling the two names is a ruling-shaped question, NOT settled here. Enforcement remains ABSENT — no gate reads the 44 (declared #200 pitfall c, unchanged by s201-D2/D3).
